heroHeadline: Russia Warns Armed Provocations Against Transnistria Would Be Treated as Attack on Russia as Citizenship Applications Top 60,000
heroSubtitle: Since Putin's May 15 decree fast-tracking Russian citizenship for Transnistria's roughly 220,000 residents and authorising presidential use of force abroad, pressure on Moldova has escalated: Prime Minister Alexandru Munteanu resigned on July 3, collapsing the pro-EU coalition, and a wave of drone incursions in August culminated in a Russian drone crossing from Moldova into Romania on August 16. On August 10 Deputy Foreign Minister Galuzin warned any armed provocation against Transnistria would be treated as an attack on Russia, as Tiraspol reported over 60,000 residents had applied for Russian citizenship under the simplified procedure — a figure Moscow moved on August 20 to keep growing by reversing a tenfold consular fee hike.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
